identity.title: Melena on digital rectal exam, or reported black tarry stool / hematemesis

technique.how: Ask about black, tarry, sticky, foul-smelling stool and any hematemesis or coffee-ground emesis, and about iron, bismuth or recent NSAID/anticoagulant use. Perform a digital rectal exam and inspect the glove: melena is black, tarry and glistening; distinguish from formed dark stool and from red blood or clots.
technique.prerequisites: Patient consent and privacy; gloves; adequate light to inspect stool colour.
technique.contraindications: Relative: severe neutropenia, recent anorectal surgery, or patient refusal; never delay resuscitation for the exam.

interpretation.positive_finding: Melenic stool on examination strongly indicates an upper GI source (LR 25), and reported melena moderately so (LR 5.1-5.9); in a patient with syncope or hypotension it establishes hemorrhage as the likely cause.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of melena does not exclude UGIB (brisk bleeds present as hematochezia); blood clots in stool argue against an upper source (LR 0.05).
interpretation.pitfalls: Iron and bismuth cause black non-tarry stool; melena requires roughly 50 mL of blood and ~8 h of transit, so early or very brisk bleeds may not yet show it. Melena localizes the source but does not by itself grade severity.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: treat as UGIB (IV access, type and screen, PPI, early endoscopy, Glasgow-Blatchford risk stratification); clots or bright red blood redirect to a lower source.

estimates.target_condition: Upper GI bleeding (vs lower GI source); finding = melenic stool on examination
estimates.population: Adults admitted or evaluated in ED with acute GI bleeding (8 studies of UGIB vs LGIB; N=1776)

estimates.target_condition: Upper GI bleeding (vs lower GI source); finding = patient-reported history of melena
estimates.population: Adults with acute GI bleeding, studies of UGIB vs LGIB localization
estimates.quote: a patient-reported history of melena (LR range, 5.1-5.9)
estimates.location: Abstract, Results (reported as a range across studies, 5.1-5.9, not a CI; lower bound entered as value)

estimates.target_condition: Upper GI bleeding (vs lower GI source); finding = blood clots in stool (present)
estimates.population: Adults with acute GI bleeding, studies of UGIB vs LGIB localization
estimates.quote: the presence of blood clots in stool (LR, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.01-0.38) decreases the likelihood of a UGIB
estimates.location: Abstract, Results (LR for presence of clots, i.e. finding present argues against UGIB)

sources.citation: Srygley FD, Gerardo CJ, Tran T, Fisher DA. Does this patient have a severe upper gastrointestinal bleed? JAMA. 2012;307(10):1072-1079.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use absence of melena to exclude significant bleeding in a hypotensive or syncopal patient, or attribute black stool to bleeding without excluding iron/bismuth.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Melena with tachycardia, hypotension, hemoglobin <8 g/dL, cirrhosis or anticoagulation indicates severe UGIB: two large-bore IVs, blood products, urgent GI endoscopy and monitored bed.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: RCE 2012 pooled LR for melena on exam has a very wide CI (4-174) reflecting few studies; reported melena varies with patient recall and stool inspection.

extraction_notes: All estimates from the Srygley 2012 JAMA RCE abstract; sensitivity/specificity for melena are not reported in the abstract and full text is not open access, so left null. Reported-melena LR is given as a range (5.1-5.9) across studies, entered as value 5.1 with no CI rather than averaged. Severity markers (tachycardia LR 4.9, Hb <8 LR 4.5-6.2, Blatchford 0 LR 0.02) belong to the severity question and are mentioned only in escalation_warning. NSAID-history RCE (PMID 16595759) was not fetched within budget and is not cited.
